title: Indivisible Greater Portland holds rally to encourage midterm voting

tea.why: Participants gathered to encourage early voting in the midterm elections and register dissent against administration policies.
tea.want: Protesters wanted to urge early voting and support Democratic candidates to shift representation in the U.S. Senate.
tea.changed: Oct 17: Hundreds gathered in Deering Oaks Park to hear speeches from Democratic candidates and federal lawmakers.

summary: On October 17, 2026, about 400 individuals assembled at Deering Oaks Park in Portland, Maine, for a rally organized by Indivisible Greater Portland. The event coincided with the national "No Kings" day of action, focusing on encouraging early voting in the upcoming midterm elections. Speakers at the gathering included Democratic gubernatorial candidate Hannah Pingree, U.S. Senate candidate Troy Jackson, and U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, who criticized Republican incumbent Senator Susan Collins and discussed issues such as healthcare, immigration, and affordability.
